related_questions.question: What is the downside of taking Paxlovid?
related_questions.snippet: The most common side effects of taking Paxlovid include impaired sense of taste (for example, a metallic taste in the mouth) and diarrhea, according to the FDA. Most people who take Paxlovid should not experience serious side effects, explains Dr. Roberts. “Paxlovid is usually very well-tolerated,” he says.

text_blocks.snippet: The Pfizer COVID-19 pill is an antiviral medication called Paxlovid (nirmatrelvir/ritonavir). It is an oral treatment for mild to moderate COVID-19 infections in adults and children over 12 years of age who are at high risk of developing severe illness, hospitalization, or death.

list.snippet: Indications: Treatment of mild to moderate COVID-19 in high-risk individuals
Dosage: Two tablets taken twice daily for five days
Reduces the risk of hospitalization or death by up to 89% when taken within three days of symptom onset
Can help prevent severe illness in high-risk patients
Not suitable for everyone, including those with certain liver or kidney conditions
Should be taken under the supervision of a healthcare professional

text_blocks.snippet: Paxlovid is available by prescription only. It is important to consult with a healthcare provider to determine if it is an appropriate treatment option.
